compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
Bug `misogynic-scheelite-solitaire` (ac3b-c6cd-8076-4a98, `1fce28eaf9b`) attaches `coverage.build_drift` (build and pinned SHAs, distance, and the remedy: update the checkout and run `make install`) to a gate verdict whose model never ran. Only the JSON output shows it, and the stderr degrade line points at the wrong cause.

Reproduced 2026-11-13 in a throwaway clone: running build `aa1681bb531`, attested config 2 commits ahead naming a Bedrock model id that does not exist, `rebar review-plan <id> --ref <sha>`:
- `--output=json`: verdict INDETERMINATE, `coverage.llm_ran=false`, `coverage.llm_error` holds the provider message, and `coverage.build_drift.remedy` = "this rebar build (aa1681bb5) is 2 commit(s) behind the config this gate read (37d8a50ab); update the checkout … and run `make install`, then re-run the gate". Correct.
- `--output=text` (the default an operator reads): only `PLAN REVIEW: INDETERMINATE`, the counts line and the source line. No build-drift line, no remedy, no provider error.
- stderr: `llm-degrade: CHANGE_SETTINGS — The request exceeded a configured bound (tokens/steps/timeout) — adjust it and retry.` The provider said `The provided model identifier is invalid` (400 ValidationException). `src/rebar/llm/failure.py` `_map_http` maps 401/403 and every non-context-length 400 to `CHANGE_SETTINGS`, and `classify_llm_failure` maps pydantic-ai `UserError` there too, but `RESOLUTION_MESSAGES[CHANGE_SETTINGS]` describes only the bound case, so it sends the operator to tokens/steps/timeout.

## Approach
1. `src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py`: add a helper `_render_model_never_ran(result)` called from `_render_plan_review_text` right after `_render_step_failures`. When `coverage.llm_ran is False` it prints `  model did not run: <coverage.llm_error, first 300 chars>` (when present). When `coverage.build_drift` is a dict with a `remedy`, it prints `  build drift: <remedy>`. A clean run (`llm_ran` true or absent) prints neither line. Extracting a helper keeps `_render_plan_review_text` under its complexity ceiling.
2. `src/rebar/llm/failure.py`: reword `RESOLUTION_MESSAGES[CHANGE_SETTINGS]` to cover what the class actually holds: "The provider rejected the request because of a setting (credentials, the model id, or a request parameter such as a token/step/timeout bound) — check the configured model, credentials and bounds, then retry." Classification does not change.
No new config key, env var or flag. JSON output is unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A text-mode plan-review result whose `coverage` holds `llm_ran: false` and `build_drift` prints a `build drift:` line containing the remedy text (including `make install`); proved by a new test in `tests/unit/test_llm_commands_render.py`.
- [ ] The same result prints a `model did not run:` line containing the `llm_error` provider message; proved by the same test file.
- [ ] A result with `llm_ran` true and no `build_drift` prints neither line (no change to clean output); proved by the same test file.
- [ ] `message_for("CHANGE_SETTINGS")` mentions the model id and credentials as well as the bounds; proved by a new assertion in `tests/unit/test_llm_disposition_plumbing.py`, and `pytest tests/unit/test_llm_disposition_plumbing.py tests/unit/test_llm_commands_render.py tests/unit/test_build_drift_degraded_verdict.py` passes.

## Testing
Write the RED tests first in `tests/unit/test_llm_commands_render.py` (degraded result with and without build drift, and a clean result) and `tests/unit/test_llm_disposition_plumbing.py` (message wording), confirm they fail, then implement. Run the 3 test files above and `make verify`.
